statement: The system shall ingest local module handbooks, past papers, and lecture slide decks in PDF, PPTX, DOCX, or Markdown format together with `pipeline.config.json`, supplying rendered slide page images alongside normalized extracted text and decoded LaTeXiT equation source (`**(Proposal for CP2)**: LaTeXiT metadata decoding`).

The system shall read course files, pages, assignments, announcements, and syllabi for in-scope modules directly from HKUST Canvas in read-only mode using the student's configured Canvas session or API token, falling back to local folder ingestion when Canvas access is unavailable.

The system shall run the Extractor agent before any Creator agent on a module to produce `glossary.json`, containing each symbol or abbreviation's full term, `standard` vs `module_specific` classification, source definition location, and canonical `"full term (abbreviation)"` or `"full term (symbol in this module)"` string.

The system shall extract module deadlines and assessment records into `deadlines.json` with title, type, UTC due datetime (`null` with a reason when unannounced), timezone, weighting, submission method, covered lectures, source location, and `explicit` vs `inferred` confidence.

The system shall extract module readings into `readings.json` with citation, page range, `required` vs `recommended` flag, linked lecture, `read_by` date defaulting to the linked lecture date, and source location.

The system shall order pipeline processing with the Computer Science modules (Theory of Computation, Machine Learning, Large Language Models) before other in-scope modules, and within each module order lectures covered by the nearest upcoming assessment before later lectures.

The system shall run a Card Creator agent per lecture to produce `concept-map.json` containing 8 to 20 concepts, each with a stable `id`, a one-line `summary`, a `source` citation, and an `importance` rating (`core`, `supporting`, or `detail`).

The system shall run the Card Creator agent per lecture to draft 15 to 40 atomic flashcards (`basic`, `cloze`, or `reverse`) in `cards.draft.json` that cite their source location and follow the 10 flashcard rules (`BR-007`–`BR-010`), diverting any unclear or contradictory source points to `flagged.json` without generating cards for them.

The system shall evaluate each lecture's draft flashcards in a fresh, independent Card Reviewer subagent instance that never receives the Card Creator's reasoning, executing Pass 1 (the blind-answer test on card fronts only) followed by Pass 2 (evaluating the 8 pass/fail card rubric criteria, recording `failed[]` criteria, and checking concept-map coverage to assign `accept`, `revise`, or `reject` verdicts in `cards.review.r<n>.json`).

The system shall cap the Card Creator–Card Reviewer loop at 2 revision rounds (up to 3 review rounds total), freezing `accept` cards, removing `reject` cards, revising only `revise` cards and `missing_concepts`, and routing any item still failing after round 3 into `flagged.json`.

The system shall run a Question Creator agent per lecture—starting only after Stage A produces a reviewed concept map—to draft question variants per concept (`3–5` for `core`, `2–3` for `supporting`, `0–1` for `detail`, using the upper bound when in the next assessment's scope) that differ in scenario, numbers, angle, or reasoning direction.

The system shall weight each lecture's generated question types (`mcq`, `short_answer`, `calculation`, `explain`, `compare`, `scenario`, `essay_plan`) according to the target assessment's format in `pipeline.config.json` (or a balanced default mix of MCQ and short-written types when the format is unannounced, per `Q-16` / `DEC-014` / `ASM-047`), including 2–5 `marking_points` for written questions, distractor explanations for MCQs, a difficulty rating (`1`–`3`), and a source citation.

The system shall evaluate each lecture's draft questions in a fresh, independent Question Reviewer subagent instance that never receives the Question Creator's reasoning, executing Pass 1 (the blind-answer test on question stems and MCQ options only) followed by Pass 2 (evaluating the 8 pass/fail question rubric criteria, recording `failed[]` criteria, and checking `core` variant counts to assign `accept`, `revise`, or `reject` verdicts in `questions.review.r<n>.json`).

The system shall cap the Question Creator–Question Reviewer loop at 2 revision rounds (up to 3 review rounds total), freezing `accept` questions, removing `reject` questions, revising only `revise` questions, and routing any question still failing after round 3 into `flagged.json`.

The system shall run the Module Auditor agent after all lectures in a module complete Stages A and B to write `module-audit.json`, recording learning-outcome coverage gaps, assessment-scope variant sufficiency, cross-lecture duplicate items, and glossary notation deviations.

The system shall route any cross-lecture synthesis cards and questions proposed by the Module Auditor through a fresh independent Reviewer instance before including accepted items in the module output.

The system shall present a pre-export human review step displaying every lecture's `flagged.json` items, `module_specific` glossary entries for confirmation, `inferred` deadlines and readings for confirmation, and a random spot-check sample of `human_spot_check_rate` (default 10%) of accepted cards and questions per lecture.

The system shall export `deck.json`, `question-bank.json`, `concepts.json`, `glossary.json`, `deadlines.json`, and `readings.json` with deterministic, stable item IDs across re-runs so that updating a lecture updates existing items in place.
The system shall write a pipeline run summary report after each run recording the counts of accepted, rejected, and flagged cards and questions per lecture alongside the module audit summary.

The system shall ingest reported items (`kind = "reported"`) exported from the study app in `R1`, routing each reported card or question with the student's comment to the relevant Creator and a fresh Reviewer in the next pipeline run.

The system shall validate uploaded pipeline export files (`deck.json`, `question-bank.json`, `concepts.json`, `glossary.json`, `deadlines.json`, `readings.json`) against their schemas to present a diff preview of new, changed, and removed items before any database write occurs.

The system shall match re-imported items by their stable `id`, updating content fields on changed items while preserving their existing `CardState`, `CardReviewLog`, `ConceptState`, and `QuestionAttempt` history.

The system shall suspend (`suspended = true`, without deletion) any previously imported card or question absent from a lecture re-import, recording an `ImportBatch` audit entry (`module_id`, `lecture_ids`, `file_kind`, `imported_at`) for the import (`**(Proposal for CP2)**: ImportBatch logging for SM-1`).

The system shall organise flashcards by `Module → Lecture → Concept → Cards` with tag filtering, rendering `basic`, `cloze`, and `reverse` cards with Markdown, KaTeX mathematics, and post-answer `extra` text.

The system shall provide flashcard review controls to reveal the card back (`Space` shortcut), rate recall as `Again` (`1`), `Hard` (`2`), `Good` (`3`), or `Easy` (`4`), or suspend, flag, or edit the active card.

The system shall compute the updated `CardState` on each flashcard rating via `ts-fsrs` (with default desired retention `0.90` and SM-2 fallback), persisting a `CardReviewLog` entry with `card_id`, `rating`, `state_before`, `reviewed_at`, and `duration_ms` (`**(Proposal for CP2)**: logging state_before for SM-2`).
The system shall enforce configurable per-module daily limits on new flashcards introduced (default 20) and due flashcard reviews (default 200).
The system shall provide a searchable notation glossary view per module displaying each `GlossaryEntry` with `module_specific` entries highlighted and confirmable by the student.
The system shall select due concepts (`ConceptState.due <= end_of_today`) per module up to the daily quiz limit (`quiz_per_day`, default 10) using each concept's independent FSRS `ConceptState`.

The system shall select a question variant for each due concept by excluding `flagged` and `suspended` questions, preferring never-seen variants over least-recently-seen variants, and breaking ties by closeness to the stability-based target difficulty (`1` if stability < 7 d, `2` if < 30 d, `3` if ≥ 30 d).
The system shall select the least-recently-seen non-flagged variant when all non-flagged variants of a due concept have already been seen, enqueueing a `topup` `FeedbackItem` for that concept.
The system shall mark `mcq` quiz responses automatically against the single correct option, revealing the model answer alongside the explanation for each distractor upon submission.

The system shall support self-marking of written and calculation quiz responses (`short_answer`, `calculation`, `explain`, `compare`, `scenario`, `essay_plan`) against the displayed `model_answer` and `marking_points`.

The system shall update `ConceptState` via `ts-fsrs` from each marked `QuestionAttempt` mapped to `Again` (wrong/no points met), `Hard` (partial points met), `Good` (correct), or `Easy` (correct, quick, and marked easy), offering immediate review of the concept's linked flashcards (`card_ids`) whenever the attempt is rated `Again`.

The system shall display module deadlines with live countdowns (days, plus hours and minutes when under 48 hours remain) and urgency indicators (`> 14 d` neutral, `7–14 d` amber, `< 7 d` red, overdue grey with a `Submitted?` checkbox) that include non-colour labels or icons.

The system shall persist student-created deadlines and manual field edits on any deadline (`title`, `module_id`, `type`, `due_at`, `timezone`, `weighting`, `submission_url`, `covers_lectures`, `notes`, `status`) with precedence over pipeline-extracted values across subsequent re-imports.
The system shall display a `Confirm` badge on extracted deadlines with `confidence = "inferred"` until the student confirms or edits them.

The system shall store all timestamps in UTC while preserving each deadline's original `timezone` (defaulting to `Asia/Hong_Kong`, `ASM-022`), so deadline times remain accurate when the student changes local timezone.

The system shall generate a `DailyPlan` ("Today" checklist) at local midnight (or on first open each day in `Settings.timezone`) ordered as: (1) carried-over unfinished items, (2) due flashcard reviews per module, (3) due concept quizzes per module, (4) daily new cards per module, (5) required readings within `reading_lookahead_days` (default 3 days), (6) deadline milestones due today, (7) assessment prep when in assessment mode, (8) recommended readings (optional, collapsed by default), and (9) student tasks.

The system shall track each `DailyPlanItem` with its formula-derived estimated duration (8 s per due card, 25 s per new card, 45 s per MCQ, 3 min per written question, `page_count × minutes_per_page` per reading) together with its `done` status and `completed_at` timestamp when checked off (`**(Proposal for CP2)**: recording completed_at for SM-4b`).
The system shall maintain student-managed checklist entries comprising module/week reading statuses (`unread`, `done`, `skimmed`, `skipped`) and personal study `Task` items.

The system shall record student-reported flashcards or quiz questions as `FeedbackItem` entries (`kind = "reported"`, `reason` set to `"wrong"` or `"unclear"`, plus comment) for export to JSON before the next pipeline run (`**(Proposal for CP2)**: structured wrong/unclear reason for SM-3`).

The system shall mark written (`short_answer`, `explain`, `scenario`, `compare`, `essay_plan`) and `calculation` quiz answers via the Claude API against the question's `marking_points`, `model_answer`, and module `glossary`, returning the indices of `points_met`, the model answer, a short feedback comment, and a suggested FSRS rating.
The system shall allow the student to override the automatic or Claude-assigned rating on any `QuestionAttempt` (`overridden = true`), updating `ConceptState` to reflect the overridden rating.

The system shall allow the student to open a Claude tutor thread from the Tutor screen or via `"Ask Claude"` on any card, quiz question, quiz result, or reading, automatically loading the item, the student's response, the marking scheme, the cited source slides, the module glossary, the student's weakest concepts (lowest stability and most lapses), and upcoming assessments.

The system shall stream Claude tutor responses in the student's selected mode (`explain`, `socratic`, or `quiz_me`), grounding answers in the course material with slide/page citations, using canonical glossary notation, and stating explicitly whenever an explanation goes beyond the course or differs from standard treatments.
The system shall send each module's glossary and extracted slide text as a cached prompt prefix on Claude marking and tutor API calls to reduce token cost and latency.

The system shall enforce the configured monthly Claude API spend threshold (`Settings.monthly_spend_cap_usd`, warning or blocking when reached) using the input tokens, output tokens, and computed USD cost logged on each `TutorMessage` and `GradingCallLog` record (`**(Proposal for CP2)**: GradingCallLog token logging and token_rates_json for SM-6`).

The system shall manage candidate flashcards and quiz questions proposed during tutor chats in a `Proposal` queue where the student can `accept`, `edit`, or `discard` each item into `feedback.json → proposed`.

The system shall route accepted tutor proposals (`feedback.json → proposed`) in the pipeline directly to a fresh independent Card or Question Reviewer subagent, invoking the corresponding Creator only if the Reviewer requires revision.

The system shall refuse requests in the Claude tutor to write or rewrite submittable prose or code for assessed coursework deadlines (`type` in `homework`, `project`, `coursework`), restricting assistance to conceptual explanation and reasoning feedback.

The system shall maintain searchable per-module `TutorThread` and `TutorMessage` history with support for deleting individual threads (`**(Proposal for CP2)**: per-thread deletion retention rule ASM-023`).

The system shall activate assessment mode for any module with an exam or midterm within `assessment_mode_days` (default 21 days), prioritising concepts in that assessment's scope sorted by lowest stability in daily quizzes, raising the module's daily new-card allowance, and adding assessment prep to the Today checklist.
The system shall run timed mock exams in assessment mode weighted to the target assessment's question-type format, producing a concept-level marked results report upon submission or timer expiry.

The system shall apply the configurable daily study time budget (`daily_budget_min`) to the Today checklist by deferring `optional` items when total estimated duration exceeds the budget while retaining all required items with an over-budget warning when required items alone exceed the budget.

The system shall allow the student to define backward-counted coursework `Milestone` steps on any deadline (`title`, `due_on`, `est_minutes`, `done`) that automatically join the Today checklist on their `due_on` date.
The system shall export module deadlines and coursework milestones as a standard iCalendar (`.ics`) file and feed (`GET /calendar.ics`) for external calendar applications.

The system shall display a Stats page showing reviews per day, trailing 30-day true retention (`SM-2`), reported-wrong item rate per module (`SM-3`), concept mastery and ≥2-attempt coverage per assessment's scope (`SM-5`), and current calendar month Claude API spend (`SM-6`).

The system shall protect all routes and API endpoints of the study app behind a single configured owner password when deployed in hosted mode (`R3`), while requiring no login when run locally (`R1`–`R2`).
The system shall operate as an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) supporting offline flashcard review, MCQ quizzes, and written-answer self-marking from cached local state.

The system shall queue written quiz answers submitted for Claude marking while offline (`grader = "pending_claude"`), automatically submitting them for Claude marking when network connectivity is restored.
The system shall send browser notifications when daily reviews are due or when an unsubmitted deadline is within 24 hours.

The system shall export the complete `feedback.json` file containing `reported` cards and questions, `topup` concepts running low on unseen variants, and `proposed` items accepted from tutor chats (`GET /export/feedback`), marking exported `FeedbackItem` rows `exported = true`.

The system shall execute a pipeline top-up run when given `feedback.json → topup` concepts, invoking only the Question Creator and a fresh Question Reviewer to generate additional distinct variants for those concepts.
The system shall compute a per-module daily review-load forecast on the Stats page using custom FSRS parameters fitted to the student's `CardReviewLog` history.
The system shall export accepted flashcards to an Anki-compatible tab-separated values file (`deck.anki.tsv`) formatted as `front<TAB>back<TAB>tags`.

**Card flip and rating latency `**(Proposal for CP2)**`:** The system shall complete a flashcard flip (`front → back`) and a rating submission (`POST /review/:cardId` plus UI transition) with p95 latency ≤ 100 ms on a local database containing 3,000 cards and 100,000 review log rows.
verification_method: Automated benchmark test in `A53` (`TC-S-N01`) measuring 200 sequential card flip and rating operations against a seeded 3,000-card / 100,000-log SQLite database.

statement: **Next card or quiz question latency `**(Proposal for CP2)**`:** The system shall return and render the next due flashcard (`GET /review/next`) or due concept quiz variant (`GET /quiz/next`) with p95 latency ≤ 300 ms on a local database of 3,000 cards, 1,000 concepts, and 4,000 questions.
verification_method: Automated benchmark test in `A53` (`TC-S-N02`) measuring 100 calls each to `/review/next` and `/quiz/next` on the seeded semester dataset.

statement: **Today checklist load time `**(Proposal for CP2)**`:** The system shall generate and render the Today checklist (`GET /today` + initial screen render) in ≤ 1,000 ms (p95) across 6 modules, 3,000 cards, 4,000 questions, 50 deadlines, and 100 readings.
verification_method: Automated system benchmark in `A53` (`TC-S-N03`) measuring full `/today` generation and DOM render time across 50 runs on the seeded dataset.

statement: **Claude written-answer marking latency `**(Proposal for CP2)**`:** The system shall return a structured Claude marking result (`POST /quiz/:questionId`) within ≤ 10.0 s (p90) under normal Anthropic API availability when using prompt caching.
verification_method: Live integration timing log check in `A53` (`TC-S-N04`) across ≥ 10 marking calls with cached module prefix, plus client timeout handling test at 10 s.

statement: **Claude tutor time-to-first-token `**(Proposal for CP2)**`:** The system shall stream the first response token from the Claude tutor (`POST /tutor/threads/:id/messages`) within ≤ 3.0 s (p90) under normal Anthropic API availability when using prompt caching.
verification_method: Live integration streaming check in `A53` (`TC-S-N05`) measuring elapsed time from request dispatch to first SSE content delta across ≥ 10 tutor messages.

statement: **Pipeline lecture processing duration `**(Proposal for CP2)**`:** The system shall complete all per-lecture pipeline stages (slide ingestion, Stage A Card Creator + Reviewer loop, Stage B Question Creator + Reviewer loop) for a single 60-slide lecture within ≤ 15 minutes of elapsed run time when not rate-limited.
verification_method: Timed end-to-end execution of `SL-01`/`SL-05` on the 61-page sample lecture (`TC-S-N06` in `A53`), recording wall-clock start and finish timestamps.

statement: **Multi-semester data volume:** The system shall store and query up to 24 modules, 12,000 flashcards, 16,000 question variants, and 500,000 `CardReviewLog` and `QuestionAttempt` rows (4 years of degree history, `[SEED §4]`) while still meeting `REQ-N-001`–`REQ-N-003`.
verification_method: Volume test in `A53` (`TC-S-N07`) seeding 12,000 cards, 16,000 questions, and 500,000 review logs and re-running `TC-S-N01`–`TC-S-N03`.

statement: **Local zero-external-dependency operation (`R1`):** The system shall run all `R1` study app workflows (`Today`, `Review`, `Quiz` with MCQ and self-marking, `Deadlines`, `Readings`, `Glossary`, `Import/Export`) on `localhost` with `0` outbound network requests required (`100%` success rate with network disabled).
verification_method: Network-isolated system test in `A53` (`TC-S-N08`) running the full `R1` acceptance suite with outbound network interfaces blocked.

statement: **PWA offline operation and queue recovery (`R3`):** When installed as a PWA in `R3`, the system shall serve `Today`, `Review`, `Quiz` (MCQ and self-marked), and `Pending` written-answer queueing with `100%` functional success while offline, flushing `100%` of queued written answers within ≤ 30 s of reconnecting.
verification_method: Playwright offline/online transition test in `A53` (`TC-S-N09`) toggling offline mode, completing card reviews and written answers, re-enabling network, and verifying sync.

statement: **FSRS mathematical fidelity:** The system shall delegate all flashcard and concept interval/stability/difficulty calculations to `ts-fsrs` such that `100%` of scheduling transitions match reference `ts-fsrs` outputs for identical input states, ratings, and timestamps.
verification_method: Deterministic unit/integration test suite (`TC-I-N10`) comparing app scheduling transitions against direct `ts-fsrs` reference vectors across all 4 states and 4 ratings.

statement: **Crash-safe persistence and pre-import backup:** The system shall protect study records against data loss via atomic database transactions (SQLite WAL with `FULL` synchronous durability or equivalent) combined with a verified pre-import backup snapshot, achieving `0` lost `CardReviewLog` or `QuestionAttempt` rows across simulated mid-write process kills (`SIGKILL`) and failed imports.
verification_method: Recovery test in `A53` (`TC-S-N11`) killing the server process mid-import and mid-review with `SIGKILL`, restarting, and verifying zero committed-log loss and clean backup restore.

statement: **Pipeline reviewer independence and quality threshold:** The pipeline shall enforce `100%` Reviewer context isolation (`0` Creator reasoning tokens or prior-round Reviewer transcripts passed to any Reviewer subagent) to achieve ≥ 95% notation compliance, ≥ 95% source citation accuracy, and `0` unflagged context-dependent cards reaching `cards.final.json` on the `A42` evaluation set.
verification_method: Automated context-payload inspection test (`TC-I-N12`) on Reviewer subagent invocations plus execution of the `A42` evaluation benchmark recorded in `A53`.

statement: **Server-only secrets and zero secret leakage:** The system shall read the Claude API key and Canvas credentials exclusively from server-side environment variables or local OS credential files outside the repository, exposing `0` secret bytes in browser responses, client bundles, logs, or git-tracked files.
verification_method: Automated bundle/response/repo scan test (`TC-S-N13`) checking built frontend assets, all API responses, log outputs, and git working tree against canary secret strings.

statement: **Prompt-injection containment:** The pipeline and study app shall encapsulate all course material text, slide text, and Canvas content inside delimited untrusted-data blocks with explicit system instructions that untrusted content can never override rules or invoke tools, achieving `100%` rejection of adversarial prompt-injection payloads in the security test suite.
verification_method: Adversarial prompt-injection test suite (`TC-S-N14` in `A39`/`A53`) injecting instruction-override, rubric-bypass, and file-write payloads into synthetic slide/Canvas fixtures.

statement: **Hosted authentication enforcement (`R3`):** When hosted mode is enabled, the server shall reject `100%` of unauthenticated HTTP requests (returning `401 Unauthorized` before invoking any database write or Claude API call) with failed password attempts rate-limited to ≤ 5 attempts per minute per IP.
verification_method: Automated security test (`TC-S-N15` in `A53`) probing every API route without a valid session and firing 10 rapid bad-password requests.

statement: **Copyrighted course material and third-party PII exclusion:** The repository and application logs shall contain `0` committed course files (`.pdf`, `.pptx`, `.docx` from course folders), `0` logged slide passages, and `0` records of other students' or Canvas discussions/rosters data.
verification_method: Pre-commit / CI guard script and test (`TC-S-N16`) verifying file-type exclusions, Canvas scope filters (`ASM-049`), and log redaction rules.

statement: **Pipeline intermediate file lifecycle `**(Proposal for CP2)**`:** The system shall store pipeline intermediate files (`*.draft.json`, `*.review.r*.json`) outside the public repository with a module-completion cleanup command that purges intermediate files while retaining exported files and review history.
verification_method: Integration test (`TC-I-N17`) running the cleanup command on a fixture module directory and verifying intermediate files are removed while exports remain intact.

statement: **WCAG 2.2 Level AA compliance:** Every screen of the study app shall achieve `0` critical or serious accessibility violations under automated WCAG 2.2 AA auditing (`axe-core`), maintain ≥ 4.5:1 text contrast, and convey deadline urgency using both text/icon badges and colour.
verification_method: Automated `axe-core` test across all rendered screens (`TC-S-N18` in `A53`) plus assertion that every deadline countdown renders an explicit text/icon urgency label.

statement: **Full keyboard operability for review and quiz:** The study app shall allow a user to complete an entire flashcard review session (`Space` to reveal, `1`–`4` to rate, `r` to report, `f` to flag) and MCQ quiz session using only the keyboard with visible focus indicators on `100%` of interactive elements.
verification_method: Automated keyboard-only end-to-end test (`TC-S-N19`) completing a 10-card review and 5-question quiz with pointer events disabled.

statement: **Schema-validated pipeline-to-app contract:** All 6 pipeline export files and `feedback.json` shall validate against versioned JSON Schemas (`A34`) with `100%` validation coverage on both pipeline export and app import, rejecting malformed payloads with field-level error messages.
verification_method: Contract test suite (`TC-I-N20` in `A39`) testing valid exports and mutated invalid payloads against the shared JSON Schemas.

statement: **Cross-browser and responsive viewport support:** All study app screens shall render without horizontal overflow and pass functional smoke tests at mobile (`375×812`) and desktop (`1280×800`) viewports in current Chromium, WebKit (Safari), and Firefox engines.

**Native Claude Code execution without OAuth extraction:** The generation pipeline shall execute as native Claude Code commands and subagent definitions invoked interactively by the student within the official Claude Code CLI, performing `0` extraction or external replay of consumer subscription OAuth tokens.
verification_method: Static inspection and architectural check (`TC-S-N22`) verifying pipeline scripts invoke only local validation/extraction utilities and native Claude Code subagent definitions.

statement: **Coursework academic integrity enforcement:** The Claude tutor shall refuse `100%` of test prompts asking it to write, complete, paraphrase for submission, or solve assessed coursework assignments (`homework`, `project`, `coursework`), offering Socratic questions or conceptual explanations instead.
verification_method: Adversarial academic-integrity test suite (`TC-S-N23` in `A53`) testing ≥ 10 direct and indirect coursework-writing prompts on a `coursework`-linked thread.
